topics.title: Fundamentals
topics.description: Microservices is an architectural style that structures an application as a collection of small, independent services that communicate over well-defined APIs. Each service focuses on a specific business capability, is independently deployable, loosely coupled, and owned by a small team. Unlike a monolith where all functionality lives in a single codebase, microservices decompose the application into smaller pieces that can be developed, deployed and scaled independently.

key_characteristics.name: Service Independence
key_characteristics.description: Each service can be developed, deployed and scaled independently.

key_characteristics.name: Decentralized Data Management
key_characteristics.description: Each service manages its own database.

key_characteristics.name: Resilience
key_characteristics.description: Failure in one service does not cascade to others.

key_characteristics.name: Scalability
key_characteristics.description: Individual services can be scaled based on demand.

key_characteristics.name: Technology Heterogeneity
key_characteristics.description: Different services can use different technologies.

topics.title: Communication
topics.description: How services talk to each other: blocking request/response, or events that decouple sender from receiver.

synchronous.name: REST APIs
synchronous.description: HTTP-based communication using JSON or XML.

synchronous.name: gRPC
synchronous.description: High-performance RPC framework using Protocol Buffers.

synchronous.name: GraphQL
synchronous.description: Query language for APIs providing clients with exactly the data they need.

topics.title: Decomposition
topics.description: How to split a system into services. Boundaries follow the business domain, not technical layers.

domain_driven_design.name: Bounded Contexts
domain_driven_design.description: Define clear boundaries between different parts of the domain.

domain_driven_design.name: Aggregates
domain_driven_design.description: Cluster of domain objects treated as a single unit.

domain_driven_design.name: Ubiquitous Language
domain_driven_design.description: Common language used by all team members.

decomposition_patterns.name: Strangler Pattern
decomposition_patterns.description: Gradually migrate a monolithic application to microservices.

topics.title: Resilience
topics.description: Patterns that stop one failing service from taking down the whole system.

patterns.name: Circuit Breaker
patterns.description: Prevents cascading failures by breaking the circuit when a service is unresponsive.

patterns.name: Bulkhead
patterns.description: Isolates failures to prevent them from cascading across the system.

patterns.name: Retry
patterns.description: Automatically retries failed operations with configurable backoff strategies.

patterns.name: Timeout
patterns.description: Sets a maximum duration for service calls to prevent indefinite waiting.

patterns.name: Rate Limiter
patterns.description: Controls the rate at which clients can access a service.

topics.title: API Gateway
topics.description: Acts as a single entry point for all clients.

responsibilities.name: Routing
responsibilities.description: Directs requests to the appropriate services.

topics.title: Service Discovery
topics.description: Enables services to find and communicate with each other without hardcoded endpoints.

approaches.name: Client-Side Discovery
approaches.description: Clients query a service registry and load balance requests themselves.

approaches.name: Server-Side Discovery
approaches.description: A router or load balancer queries the service registry on the client's behalf.

topics.title: Config & Deployment
topics.description: Centralizing configuration across services and environments, and shipping each service independently.
continuous_deployment: CI/CD pipelines for automated testing and deployment

topics.title: Observability
topics.description: You cannot debug a distributed system without tracing, aggregated logs and metrics in place from day one.

pillars.name: Distributed Tracing
pillars.description: Tracks requests as they flow through microservices.

topics.title: Advanced Patterns
topics.description: The patterns that come up once the basic decomposition is settled.

patterns.name: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
patterns.description: Separates read and write operations into different models.

patterns.name: Event Sourcing
patterns.description: Stores changes to application state as a sequence of events.

patterns.name: Saga Pattern
patterns.description: Manages distributed transactions across multiple services through a sequence of local transactions.

patterns.name: Backend for Frontend (BFF)
patterns.description: Creates dedicated backend services for specific frontend applications.

patterns.name: Sidecar Pattern
patterns.description: Deploys helper services alongside the main application container.

topics.title: Vs Monolith
topics.description: The comparison interviewers ask for, plus the costs microservices add on top.

challenges.name: Testing Complexity
challenges.description: Testing service interactions becomes more complex.

challenges.name: Team Organization
challenges.description: Requires cross-functional teams aligned with services.

topics.when_a_monolith_wins: Microservices architecture introduces complexity that should be justified by the scale and organizational requirements of your application. For smaller applications, a well-designed monolith may be more appropriate.

topics.title: Spring Cloud
topics.description: Spring Cloud provides tools for common microservices patterns.

topics.title: Best Practices
topics.description: The short list to fall back on when asked how you would do it properly.
best_practices: Design services around business capabilities, not technical functions
Choose the right size for services - not too big, not too small
Implement proper monitoring and observability from the start
Design for failure and implement resilience patterns

tips.title: Team Organization
